exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

modules.title: Use Python 3.13 replacement and batching APIs

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.13 added strict= to itertools.batched; strict=True raises ValueError when the final batch is shorter than n.

reveal.text: Python 3.13 added strict= to itertools.batched; strict=True raises ValueError when the final batch is shorter than n.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ batch in batched(records, 100, strict=True): ... enforces exact batch size.

reveal.text: for batch in batched(records, 100, strict=True): ... enforces exact batch size.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ validation happens as the iterator is consumed, because batched is lazy.

reveal.text: The validation happens as the iterator is consumed, because batched is lazy.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.13 added copy.replace(obj, **changes), a common replacement protocol supported by dataclasses, named tuples, datetime types, and custom __replace__ implementations.

reveal.text: Python 3.13 added copy.replace(obj, **changes), a common replacement protocol supported by dataclasses, named tuples, datetime types, and custom __replace__ implementations.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ = copy.replace(config, retries=5) creates a modified copy without mutating the original.

reveal.text: new_config = copy.replace(config, retries=5) creates a modified copy without mutating the original.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ is not a general deep copy; it constructs a replacement with selected fields changed.

reveal.text: copy.replace is not a general deep copy; it constructs a replacement with selected fields changed.

modules.title: Use Python 3.13 queue and typing additions

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.13 added Queue.shutdown() and the ShutDown exception for explicit producer-consumer queue termination.

reveal.text: Python 3.13 added Queue.shutdown() and the ShutDown exception for explicit producer-consumer queue termination.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________() prevents future growth while allowing already queued work to wind down normally by default.

reveal.text: q.shutdown() prevents future growth while allowing already queued work to wind down normally by default.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________(immediate=True) breaks the usual join invariant by draining work immediately, so it should be used deliberately.

reveal.text: shutdown(immediate=True) breaks the usual join invariant by draining work immediately, so it should be used deliberately.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.13 added typing.TypeIs for user-defined type-narrowing predicates whose true and false branches can both narrow more intuitively than TypeGuard.

reveal.text: Python 3.13 added typing.TypeIs for user-defined type-narrowing predicates whose true and false branches can both narrow more intuitively than TypeGuard.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ is_str(value: object) -> TypeIs[str]: return isinstance(value, str) communicates narrowing to a type checker.

reveal.text: def is_str(value: object) -> TypeIs[str]: return isinstance(value, str) communicates narrowing to a type checker.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ is a typing contract: the function's runtime boolean logic must actually satisfy the type relationship it claims.

reveal.text: TypeIs is a typing contract: the function's runtime boolean logic must actually satisfy the type relationship it claims.
